name: Marathi
where: Maharashtra — Mumbai, Pune, Nagpur and every village between — plus Goa's border belt and diaspora communities in Israel, Mauritius and the US.
script_note: The SAME script as Hindi — if you read Hindi, you can sound out Marathi on day one. Only two surprises wait: ळ (retroflex L, unknown in Hindi) and a few spelling habits of its own.
difficulty: US Foreign Service Institute Category III (about 1,100 hours to professional proficiency) — grouped with Hindi. The shared script makes reading easy; three genders where Hindi has two make grammar harder.

sov.en: I eat rice (a man speaking — a woman says खाते; word-for-word: I · rice · eat)

gender_note: Marathi has masculine, feminine AND neuter — one more than Hindi. Adjectives and verbs agree: चांगला मुलगा (good boy), चांगली मुलगी (good girl), चांगले पुस्तक (good book). Learn every noun with its gender.
present_note: The verb agrees with WHO is speaking and their gender: a man says खातो, a woman says खाते. Formal तुम्ही takes its own ending — the verb tells you the relationship.
negation_note: Put नाही (nahi) after a present-tense verb: मी जात नाही (mi jat nahi) — I don't go. Past tense keeps it after too: गेलो नाही (gelo nahi) — didn't go.
counting_note: Marathi counts directly — number + noun, no classifier words:
survival_trio: X कुठे आहे? (where is X?), भाडे किती? (how much?), इथे थांबा (stop here). These three handle 80% of travel.
bargaining_script: हे कितीला? → खूप महाग! → थोडे कमी करा → ठीक आहे, घेतो. Smile through all four steps.

vowels.hint: a as in 'about' — a short neutral uh
ru as in 'rude' — rare, Sanskrit loanwords only
breathy h at word end — rare

consonants.hint: k with a puff of air
g with a puff of air
ng as in 'sing' — rare in daily Marathi
ch with a puff of air
j with a puff of air
n as in 'inch' — rare in daily words
retroflex t with a puff of air
retroflex d with a puff of air
dental t with a puff of air (never 'th' as in 'thin')
dental d with a puff of air
p with a puff of air (often 'f' in city speech)
b with a puff of air
same sound as श in daily speech
THE Marathi sound: retroflex L, tongue curled back. बाळ (child) vs बाल (hair) — a true minimal pair

pronouns.note: आपण (āpaṇ) = we-INCLUDING-you — Marathi splits what Hindi/English merge
Three words where Hindi has one: तो/ती/ते (he/she/it)
Agrees with gender: masc / fem / neuter

verbs.note: बघणे (baghaṇe) is the Mumbai street word for 'see'
For 'I want X', use मला X पाहिजे — see daily phrases
Deep love only — for food and films use आवडणे
चहा पितो — tea is 'drunk', like Hindi

time_words.note: Yesterday ONLY — tomorrow is उद्या (Hindi/Bengali काल covers both)

food_words.note: वरण (varaṇ) is dal thinned for rice — the comfort pairing
Goat meat by default in Maharashtra
The village staple — पोळी (poḷī) is the wheat one

colors.note: Adjectives agree with gender: काळा/काळी/काळे (black m/f/n)

core_nouns.note: Same word for both — the verb shows the gender

travel_words.note: Literally 'fire-cart' — ट्रेन and रेल्वे work too

shopping_phrases.note: Street Marathi — बघणे is 'see' in Mumbai speech

daily_phrases.note: पाहिजे (want/need) always works this way: मला X पाहिजे

culture.en: Mumbai's ten-day Ganpati festival (Aug–Sep) — drums, dancing processions and modaks. Shout गणपती बाप्पा मोरया with the crowd and you're family.
Marathi New Year in spring — a decorated gudhi flag flies outside every house, and the new almanac year begins.
The barefoot pilgrimage to Pandharpur — lakhs walk for weeks singing abhangas. Maharashtra's moving heart; join even one day of it.
Fiery folk music and dance — fast drums, quicker wit. One live show teaches your ear more rhythm than a month of tapes.
Sprouted-bean curry crowned with farsan, mopped up with pav — Kolhapur's is famously incendiary. Order दही (curd) on the side if you're cautious.

classifiers.note: one book — no classifier word needed
three people — people count directly too

lines.r: Mī ṭhīk āhe, dhanyavād. Tumhī kuṭhle?
lines.hi: मैं ठीक हूँ, धन्यवाद। आप कहाँ से हैं?

Brother, one tea please. (दादा = elder brother — everyone calls the vendor दादा)
Excuse me, where is the station?

quiz.explain: नमस्कार (namaskār) is the standard formal hello — to elders, officials, anyone you respect.

quiz.q: How do you say 'thank you' in Marathi?
quiz.explain: धन्यवाद (dhanyavād). माफ करा is excuse-me/sorry — don't mix them.
ळ (ḷ) is Marathi's signature sound. बाळ (child) vs बाल (hair) — get it right and Maharashtrians will beam.
तुम्ही (tumhī) is formal 'you' — safe with every stranger.
पाच (pāc) = 5. Same root as Hindi पाँच.
वीस (vīs) = 20 — its own word, like English 'twenty'.
शंभर (śambhar) = 100. Don't confuse it with the South Indian dish sambar!
भात (bhāt) is cooked rice — uncooked rice is तांदूळ.
मासे (māse) = fish. Coastal Maharashtra runs on fish and rice.
एक = one, द्या = give (polite). The full polite ordering pattern.
कुठे (kuṭhe) = where. X कुठे आहे? is the whole direction toolkit in three words.
उजवीकडे (ujavīkaḍe) = to the right. Left is डावीकडे, straight is सरळ.
भाडे (bhāḍe) = fare, किती = how much. Ask before you sit down.

quiz.q: मी भात खातो. The word order is…
quiz.explain: Marathi is subject–object–verb: मी भात खातो. The verb always goes last.
तुम्ही (tumhī) is formal and safe everywhere. तू to a stranger is rude.
नाही after the verb negates it: खात नाही = don't eat. Simplest negation in any major language.
खाते (khāte) — Marathi verbs agree with the speaker's gender. Men say खातो.
माझे (mājhe) = my, नाव = name. माझे नाव प्रिया = my name is Priya.
शिकतोय (śiktoy) is present continuous: right now, in progress. A woman says शिकतेय. Say it to any Maharashtrian and watch them smile.
पुस्तक (pustak) = book. एक पुस्तक = one book.
घर (ghar) = house/home. घरात = at home (त = in/at).
हे (this) + कितीला (for how much). The market survival sentence.
उद्या (udyā) = tomorrow. Yesterday is काल — Marathi splits what Hindi/Bengali काल covers.
